title: How I Built ReviewMind: A History-Aware PR Reviewer (Hackathon Project)
summary: Building a history-aware GitHub pull request reviewer with IBM Bob, watsonx.ai, and pgvector for the IBM Bob 2.0 hackathon.

sections.title: The idea
paragraphs: I participated in IBM Bob 2.0, a hackathon conducted by IBM, using the Bob IDE for AI-assisted coding.
My idea was simple. On GitHub, most open-source maintainers struggle with pull request (PR) reviews, so I built a solution to help with that.

I started in Plan mode to map out how to execute the project. We were given 40 Bob coins to use the AI. Bob asked follow-up questions, finalised the plan, and broke it into 5 subtasks for its subagents to execute in Agent mode.

sections.title: How it works
paragraphs: The core idea is three review lenses: regression, API contracts, and backend pitfalls.
Before the server starts, an ingestion script reads closed pull requests and project rules and stores them for later retrieval.

When a pull request is opened, a GitHub webhook triggers the review pipeline. It fetches the diff and file list, sends the relevant context to watsonx.ai, and combines the structured findings into a review.

The design supports parallel reviews. In the implementation shown below, the three lenses run sequentially to respect watsonx.ai Lite plan rate limits; fetching the diff and file list still happens concurrently.

sections.title: 1. Regression lens and RAG
paragraphs: This lens looks for changes that could break existing behaviour. Its analysis is grounded in two sources indexed in pgvector: project rules and past pull request history.
The rules cover API design, code structure, dependencies, async performance, error handling, security, testing, and documentation. Past pull requests provide context about earlier changes.
Embeddings are generated with watsonx.ai. This ingestion function reads the project rules and GitHub pull request history, then stores the chunks in pgvector.
sections.code:
async def ingest(
    rules_path: Path,
    github_owner: str,
    github_repo: str,
    max_prs: int,
    dry_run: bool,
) -> None:
    # --- 1. Project rules ----------------------------------------------------
    rule_chunks = chunk_rules(rules_path)
    for chunk in rule_chunks:
        if dry_run:
            logger.info("[dry-run] Would upsert %s: %s…", chunk["doc_id"], chunk["text"][:80])
        else:
            logger.info("Upserting rule chunk: %s", chunk["doc_id"])
            await upsert_document(chunk["doc_id"], chunk["text"], chunk["metadata"])
    # --- 2. Past PRs ---------------------------------------------------------
    per_page = min(max_prs, 100)
    max_pages = max(1, -(-max_prs // per_page))  # ceiling division
    repo_full = f"{github_owner}/{github_repo}"  # ← moved up, defined before use
    logger.info(
        "Fetching up to %d closed PRs from %s/%s…",
        max_prs,
        github_owner,
        github_repo,
    )
    pr_chunk_count = 0
    async with GithubClient() as gh:
        prs = await gh.list_past_prs(
            github_owner, github_repo,
            per_page=per_page,
            max_pages=max_pages,
        )
        for pr in prs[:max_prs]:
            chunks = await chunk_pr_with_diff(
                gh, pr, repo_full, github_owner, github_repo
            )
            for chunk in chunks:
                if dry_run:
                    logger.info("[dry-run] %s → %s…", chunk["doc_id"], chunk["text"][:70])
                else:
                    await upsert_document(chunk["doc_id"], chunk["text"], chunk["metadata"])
                pr_chunk_count += 1
    if not dry_run:
        await close_pool()
    logger.info("Bootstrap complete. Rules: %d, PR chunks: %d", len(rule_chunks), pr_chunk_count)

sections.title: 2. API contract lens
paragraphs: This lens checks API changes against available contracts. The example looks for a specification in the changed files and falls back to an external registry when no specification is found. It prompts Granite with the diff and contract context, then parses the findings.
sections.code:
async def run(diff: str, files: list[dict]) -> LensResult:
    """
    Run the API Contract Lens against a PR diff.
    1. Look for a spec file in the changed files.
    2. Fall back to the external registry if configured and no spec found.
    3. Prompt Granite with diff + contract context.
    """
    contract_context = _extract_spec_from_files(files)
    if contract_context is None:
        registry_url = get_settings().external_api_registry_url
        contract_context = await _fetch_from_registry(registry_url)
    prompt = _build_prompt(diff, contract_context)
    raw_response = await generate(prompt)
    findings = _parse_findings(raw_response)
    passed = all(f.severity != Severity.CRITICAL for f in findings)
    logger.info(
        "API Contract lens: %d findings (%d critical)",
        len(findings),
        sum(1 for f in findings if f.severity == Severity.CRITICAL),
    )
    return LensResult(lens_name=LENS_NAME, passed=passed, findings=findings)

sections.title: 3. Backend pitfall lens
paragraphs: This lens looks for common backend anti-patterns, including N+1 queries, missing authentication or authorization, insecure defaults, poor error handling, and dependency or version drift.

sections.title: Combining the review
paragraphs: The combiner uses the findings to calculate a risk score and create a structured summary. The implementation posts a GitHub PR review with inline annotations where applicable. If inline positions are invalid, it retries with a body-only review.
The summary is included in the PR review body; this version avoids posting a duplicate top-level issue comment.
sections.code:
async def run_review_pipeline(owner: str, repo: str, pull_number: int) -> None:
    """
    Orchestrate the full PR review:
      1. Fetch diff and file list from GitHub.
      2. Run all three lenses in parallel with asyncio.gather.
      3. Compute risk score and build output.
      4. Post inline review + top-level summary comment to GitHub.
    """
    logger.info("Starting review pipeline for %s/%s PR #%d", owner, repo, pull_number)
    async with GithubClient() as gh:
        # Step 1 — fetch PR data
        try:
            diff, files = await asyncio.gather(
                gh.get_pr_diff(owner, repo, pull_number),
                gh.get_pr_files(owner, repo, pull_number),
            )
        except Exception as exc:
            logger.error("Failed to fetch PR data: %s", exc)
            return
        # Step 2 — run three lenses sequentially to respect Lite plan rate limits
        # Switch back to asyncio.gather when on a paid watsonx.ai plan
        results: list[LensResult] = []
        try:
            for coro in [
                regression_lens.run(diff, files),
                api_contract_lens.run(diff, files),
                backend_pitfall_lens.run(diff, files),
            ]:
                results.append(await coro)
        except Exception as exc:
            logger.error("Lens execution failed: %s", exc)
            return
        # Step 3 — combine
        risk_score = compute_risk_score(results)
        summary = build_summary_comment(results, risk_score)
        inline_comments = build_inline_comments(results)
        logger.info(
            "Review complete — risk score: %d, inline comments: %d",
            risk_score,
            len(inline_comments),
        )
        # Step 4 — post to GitHub as a PR review (single post, no duplicate issue comment)
        # Try with inline comments first; fall back to body-only if positions are invalid.
        try:
            await gh.post_pr_review(
                owner, repo, pull_number,
                review_body=summary,
                comments=inline_comments,
            )
            logger.info("Posted PR review with %d inline comments", len(inline_comments))
        except Exception as exc:
            logger.warning(
                "PR review with inline comments failed (%s) — retrying without inline comments", exc
            )
            try:
                await gh.post_pr_review(
                    owner, repo, pull_number,
                    review_body=summary,
                    comments=[],
                )
                logger.info("Posted PR review (no inline comments)")
            except Exception as exc2:
                logger.error("Failed to post PR review: %s", exc2)
